lesson.grammar_point: so and such for emphasis (so plus adjective, such a plus adjective plus noun, so and such ... that for a result)

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: pleasant and attractive in a small, gentle way
something good that you did not expect
to be as good as people say or as you hoped
so good or so big that you admire it
full of tourists, and made more for them than for the people who live there
not as good as you hoped

reading.rtitle: So Quiet, Such Good Wine: Three Days in the Brda Hills
paras: Everybody told me that Ljubljana was charming and that Lake Bled was impressive. They were right about Ljubljana. Bled was a different story. It was such a famous place that I could not see the lake through the selfie sticks, and the boat to the island was so expensive that I stayed on the shore. For me, Bled did not live up to the photos. It was not ugly. It was just touristy, and a little disappointing.

Then a waiter in Ljubljana gave me a tip: go west, to the Brda hills, near the Italian border. I almost said no. The bus trip was long and exhausting, and I expected a dull little village with one shop. I was so wrong. Brda was a pleasant surprise from the first hour. The villages are so small that you can walk across them in five minutes, and the people are so relaxed that nobody looks at the clock.

On the second day a family invited me to taste their wine in a room under the house. It was such a simple room: a table, six glasses and a window over the vineyards. But it was the best afternoon of the trip. Today, when people ask me about Slovenia, I don't talk about the famous lake. I talk about Brda. It was such a quiet place, and the wine was so good, that I want to go back next year.

items.situation: Ask me about my last trip, so that I react.

listenings.text: Last year I booked a table at one of the most famous restaurants in Zagreb, three months before the trip. Everybody online said it was such an impressive place. Well, honestly, it did not live up to the reviews. We waited forty minutes for our table, and the room was so noisy that I could not hear my husband. The food was beautiful on the plate, but the portions were so small that we bought a sandwich on the way back to the hotel. The next day we had lunch at a tiny place near the market, with no website and no reviews. The fish was so fresh, and the owner was such a kind man, that we went back twice. That was the real pleasant surprise of the trip.

I am not a big football fan, but in Split a friend took me to see Hajduk at the Poljud stadium. I expected a dull evening. I was wrong. The fans started singing an hour before the game, and the atmosphere was so electric that I forgot to look at the field. The game itself was not impressive. It ended zero to zero. But the people around me were such passionate fans that every pass felt like a final. After the game we walked back along the sea for an hour. It was exhausting, but it was such a good night that I bought a Hajduk scarf the next morning. Now it hangs in my office, next to my books.

extra_audio.text: First he visited Lake Bled, but the crowd was so big that he could not see the lake. Then a waiter in Ljubljana told him to go west, to the Brda hills near the Italian border. After that he took a long and exhausting bus trip, and he expected a dull little village. At that point a family invited him to taste their wine in a simple room under the house. In the end Brda was such a pleasant surprise that he wants to go back next year.
